nightly-evals-bot: ALERT: nightly evals (master) failed on 24/50 prompts in help_center_summaries — large shift in length & factuality metrics vs baseline. regression_score: -0.27 :warning:

mia: pinging eng-ml, saw the bot. failing prompts look like shorter, hallucinated summaries. any recent config/model changes? :eyes:

own: I pulled the eval run — model: rdx-2.1-quant, runners: default-serve, sampling config used: 
```json
{"temperature": 0.85, "top_p": 0.92, "top_k": 50, "seed": null}
```
That temp seems higher than our usual 0.7. who bumped it?

tara: we had a config merge yesterday to adopt 'adaptive_temp' heuristic for ad-hoc experiments, but it should only apply to the A/B cohort, not master. suspicious. I can check the deploy logs.

own: I diffed the model bundle on the host — there is a model-defaults.json in /srv/models/rdx-2.1-quant bundled with the image: 
```diff
- "temperature": 0.7
+ "temperature": 0.85  // added in bundle build 2024-11-18 by ci-build-42
```

kevin: that explains longer, looser generations. but the regression looks bigger than temp bump alone. could seed handling changed?

mia: good call. the nightly evals are deterministic except for sampling. we seed the generator per-eval with a fixed seed. If seed isn't applied consistently across code paths (top_p vs top_k), variance would spike.

own: I instrumented the runtime on a staging replica: when using the fast-path sampler (fast_sampler.cu) we were calling rng.seed() only if seed != null. but in python-serving path we pass seed=None for our eval harness and expect the runtime to use the fixed evaluation seed from eval harness. looks like the new bundle changed the parameter name from "seed" -> "rand_seed" in the config, so the C++ fast-path never saw the eval seed.

tara: ugh. config key rename in CI. that would silently drop the seed. can you repro locally?

own: repro steps: 
1) run nightly-eval harness with --eval-seed=42 against rdx-2.1-quant built bundle
2) observe outputs differ run-to-run when sampler uses fast-path
3) force config key back to "seed" and runs become deterministic again.

kevin: can you paste the small diff you used to fix on the host?

own: sure: 
```diff
--- model-defaults.json.orig
+++ model-defaults.json.fixed
@@
- "rand_seed": null,
+ "seed": 42,
  "temperature": 0.85,
  "top_p": 0.92,
  "top_k": 50
```
Note: I set seed to eval harness seed to validate behaviour, not final commit.

mia: nice. so root causes: (1) accidental temp bump in model bundle, (2) config key rename broke seed propagation to fast C++ sampler. Two separate regressions, amplified together.

tara: immediate mitigation: revert model-defaults.json to previous bundle (temp 0.7, seed key present) and re-run nightly. I'll open a rollback PR to image builder.

own: also adding a guard in the runtime: accept both "seed" and "rand_seed" keys and log a warning if both present. small patch attached to this thread.

kevin: add an e2e test to eval CI that runs the harness twice and asserts identical outputs given fixed seed and config path exercise both python and C++ sampling paths. Could add a matrix: sampler=fast, sampler=py.

mia: agreed. follow-ups: 
- tar: rollback PR and hotfix image build (P0)
- owen: runtime backward-compat patch + unit test (P0)
- kevin: add deterministic-run test in eval CI (P1)
- mia: rerun nightly eval once rollback done and confirm metrics recover, then postmortem note.

tara: creating PR now -> https://git.internal/redwood/ci-builds/pull/1234 :white_check_mark:

own: pushing runtime guard patch to review -> https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/987 :raising_hand:

kevin: putting an automatic alert on the model-bundle builder to prevent accidental default hyperparam drift (compare to last release). will follow up in infra channel.

mia: thanks all. please ping here when nightly passes. tagging @nightly-evals-bot for re-run once deploys are up. :thumbsup:

nightly-evals-bot: scheduled re-run requested by @mia — will run once the image rollback finishes and report back in this thread.
